quote: You have not done enough, you have never done enough, so long as it is still possible that you have something of value to contribute.
source: Dag Hammarskjöld, Markings (trans. Leif Sjöberg and W. H. Auden, 1964)
note: Corrected the locator. The sentence stands in the body of Markings in the Sjöberg and Auden translation, confirmed by full text search of several scans. The cited page 262 of the Vintage Spiritual Classics of 2006 could not be confirmed and that edition is shorter, so the page is dropped and the translation named instead.

evidence.where: Open Library search inside, which returns the sentence from the body of two scans of Markings and shows what follows it; the quote anthologies that print a shorter wording were checked against the book and are wrong
evidence.edition: Markings, trans. Leif Sjöberg and W. H. Auden, Alfred A. Knopf, 1964
evidence.locator: an undated entry; the next sentence reads This is the answer when you are groaning under what you consider a burden

reason: The wording is settled: the book itself reads something of value to contribute, while the widely copied something to contribute appears only in quotation anthologies. The page is not. Every scan of Markings on the Internet Archive is lending restricted, so no page number could be read, and page 262 is longer than the 2006 Vintage volume runs. Rather than print a page nobody has seen, the citation names the translation.
